def recover_from_pairwise_sums(sums):
    """
    Reconstruct a hidden integer sequence from the multiset of its pairwise sums.

    A hidden non-decreasing sequence a[0] <= a[1] <= ... <= a[n-1] of n integers
    (n >= 3) determines the n*(n-1)//2 pairwise sums a[i] + a[j] taken over all
    index pairs i < j.  You are given exactly that multiset of sums, as a list
    in arbitrary order.

    Input:
      sums -- a list of n*(n-1)//2 integers for some 3 <= n <= 40 (the length
      is guaranteed to be a triangular number of this form).  Every element
      satisfies |s| <= 2 * 10**9.  Hidden values may be negative and may repeat;
      the bound n <= 40 limits only the input size, NOT the value range, so any
      brute-force search over candidate integer sequences is unbounded.

    Output:
      The lexicographically smallest non-decreasing list of n integers whose
      multiset of pairwise sums is exactly the input multiset, or the empty
      list [] if no integer sequence realizes it.  (Distinct sequences can
      share the same sum multiset -- e.g. both [1, 4, 5, 6] and [2, 3, 4, 7]
      realize the first example below; return the lexicographically smaller,
      comparing element by element.)

    >>> recover_from_pairwise_sums([10, 5, 11, 9, 7, 6])
    [1, 4, 5, 6]
    >>> recover_from_pairwise_sums([3, 5, 4])
    [1, 2, 3]
    >>> recover_from_pairwise_sums([0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 2])
    []
    """
